result:
Round 398 is planned and dispatched as PERF-14a. The decision is **CONTINUE**: nothing external blocks the next stage, and too much scope remains for COMPLETE.

**Round 397 closed from evidence.** C passed it in a real browser on both viewports with 0 bugs, and gate 397 published commit `c93d926` on both remotes. That finishes PERF-13 and closes R314-DEMO-BUFFER-LONGTASK-6X and PERF2-STEREO-COPY. Four notes were filed without scheduling new work:
- C's Low and the gate reviewer's three Lows (ruled "keep") went to `deferred_low_polish`.
- The reviewer's architecture note is recorded as a signal only.
- The 397 task is copied to `tasks/round-397.md`.

**Why PERF-14 is split.** I measured 200 clips at HEAD on both viewports:

| Measure | Result | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Page elements | 4,294 / 4,277 | ≤ 2,000 |
| Of those, inside clips | 3,400 (17 per clip) | — |
| Clips actually in the window | 1 (default zoom), 16–19 (min zoom) | — |
| Zoom key time, normal CPU | 40–48 ms | p95 < 50 ms |
| Zoom key time, 6× slower CPU | 272–280 ms | — |

So the target fails today, and virtualization can meet it at any zoom. The ruler is already windowed, so I corrected PERF-14's outdated note saying it grows with the project. The stages are:
- **14a (this round):** a measuring harness, plus a clip count from the model.
- **14b:** clip virtualization.
- **14c:** the multi-resolution peaks and canvas drawing, plus the eight round-315 peaks Lows.

**Round 398 task** (`current-task.md`, starting from `c93d926`):
- **App change:** each lane row gets a `data-clip-count` attribute, the lane's clip count from the model rather than from the page. It is needed because 51 test and perf files currently find clips through the page, and that breaks once 14b removes off-screen clips. It changes nothing visible.
- **My trial version of that change:** five test rows (LC1–LC5), five deliberately broken versions that all fail those rows, typecheck and lint clean, and the full suite passing (260 files, 3,852 tests). `tech-lead` reviewed it twice and found nothing at Medium or above.
- **A writes** a new 200-clip perf spec with its budgets file, plus doc 254. It measures page size, mounted vs model clip counts and zoom key timing at normal and 6× CPU, at default zoom, minimum zoom and minimum zoom scrolled to the middle. Every row is record-only, because I did not run the spec myself.
- **C checks:**
  - the counts match my HEAD probe;
  - the existing resource perf rows are unchanged;
  - the attribute equals the clips on screen at every step of a real browser recipe;
  - nothing visible changed, premium routes are still protected, and only the 5 granted files changed.

**What the advisor's closing review changed.** I had written that a clip shows on its new lane while a cross-lane drag is still held. When I probed it, the clip stays on its source lane until release (3/0 while held, 2/1 after release, 3/0 after undo). The browser check now uses those measured numbers.

**Consults.** The advisor was used at the start and at close. `performance-optimizer` and `tech-lead` agreed on the order and on a separate spec file. They disagree on whether 14b keeps every selected clip mounted, since select-all would put all 200 back. That is recorded as Q-14B-PIN-SELECTED for the 14b task, not decided now.

**Next:**
- PERF-14b, then 14c, then PERF-15.
- A regression round is due at the first planning on or after 2026-11-10, and RETRO at round 400.
- The architecture checkpoint for root is still due and doesn't block this round. Before dispatching 14b I'll ask root for a bounded `frontend-architect` checkpoint on the virtualization shape, unless root has already run one.

I left the store tree untouched (clean at `c93d926`). I changed only loop files: `backlog.json` (now v365), `feature-status.md`, `current-task.md`, `b-round-397.md`, `b-next.json`, `tasks/round-397.md` and the `b-round-397/` folder.
